beats.lead: Every open-source project seems to use it
beats.note: By Jerome Saltzer's own account, the words cover a family of related licences with different wording, not one document MIT ever finalised.

beats.name: Jerome Saltzer and Larry Allen
beats.role: MIT, working with attorneys Bob Sullivan and Sib Reppert. Not for the famous X Window System; the first version was drafted for PC/IP, an obscure TCP/IP stack for the IBM PC.

beats.lead: The X Window System version came later
beats.note: A separate set of attorneys reused Saltzer's four principles for Jim Gettys and Bob Scheifler, two years after the licence type it made famous already existed.

beats.lead: Even today's version does not match
beats.text: The text OSI approved in 1999 is not the X11 wording.
beats.note: It descends from the Expat XML parser's licence instead, and drops the X11 clause restricting use of the copyright holder's name in advertising.

beats.text: The most copied licence on the internet was never actually finalised once.

beats.line: Free to reuse. Never one document.
